newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 200 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 200 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 120 billion bolivar ($247 million) auction of 177-day VE6MTMA=RR "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 20.78 percent coupon.

The bank said it would also offer 40 billion bolivars ($82 million) in 266-day bills VE9MTMA=RR with a 21.31 percent coupon, and another 40 billion bolivars of 358-day bills VE1YTMA=RR with a 21.87 percent coupon.
Nearly 100 billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday, and another 30 billion next Monday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are down from last week's 90 billion bolivar issue. Then 177-, 268- and 358-day notes carried 21.66, 22.24, and 22.84 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that fell nearly one point at the short end of the curve to 20.78 and 22.81 percent respectively, but rose at the 358-day maturity by over half a point to 22.81 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
